name: Fake member OIDC, signup and public ledger authorization world
target: Drive real member signup, browser OAuth callback, native PKCE app-slot exchange, owner and board Nexus HTTP routes, member-key handlers, and the public machine-scoped resource-ledger route using a fake Google OIDC edge and fake HTTPS VM transport
inputs: deterministic fake Google identities, authorization URL, callback state and S256 PKCE
KAIST event-code and concurrent signup requests
member plan catalog rows and app-slot lifecycle state
host-bound machine tokens, public HTTPS ledger URL and pool declarations
observations: concurrent callbacks retain separate member sessions, event-code attribution and isolated app slots
Nexus HTTP browser start, callback, native one-time code exchange and owner route preserve state and reject callback/code replay
the allowlisted elanous://auth/callback returns only an app-slot code and state; app-scoped bearer is issued only after PKCE exchange
a member cannot create a second app slot and its #36200 member key can be revoked
public HTTPS provider reads only its host pool; missing, wrong-host, expired or revoked tokens fail closed
public HTTP is rejected before the bearer is sent and successful declarations assemble a provider
